title: Liquid C2 and Graphiant Launch Managed Post-Quantum Network-as-a-Service Across Africa - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Liquid C2, the cloud and cybersecurity subsidiary of Cassava Technologies, has partnered with U.S.-based AI networking vendor Graphiant to deliver a managed Quantum Secure Network-as-a-Service (NaaS) across African enterprise and public-sector infrastructure. Rather than forcing organizations to remediate thousands of legacy applications individually against harvest-now, decrypt-later attacks, the service embeds post-quantum cryptography (PQC) directly into the transport layer linking branch offices, data centers, cloud environments, and external partners.

Built on Graphiant’s stateless edge-to-core networking architecture, the service establishes quantum-resistant tunnels using NIST Security Level 5 ML-KEM-1024 key encapsulation alongside FIPS 204 ML-DSA authentication. Centralizing cryptographic agility at the network fabric enables enterprises to rotate algorithms across connected endpoints as post-quantum standards evolve without application-level code rewrites.

The offering also addresses governance risks created by autonomous AI agents and connected devices communicating across distributed model endpoints. Network-level session tracing and destination policies restrict lateral movement by compromised agents, while country-level path enforcement and auditable transit logs allow regulated finance, government, and healthcare organizations to route sensitive workloads onto Cassava AI Factories under strict data-sovereignty mandates.
